plain: 朴素的；纯色的；未加调味的
tape: 胶带；用胶带粘；在 tape measure 中指卷尺或软尺

stories.title: Thunder for a Film
stories.picture: 两人在家用金属托盘和厚坐垫尝试制造雷声，架子上的手机正录音。
paragraphs: My cousin and I made a film about two astronauts who hear thunder inside their spacecraft.
我和表亲拍了一部短片，讲的是两名宇航员在航天器里听见雷声的故事。
Our script called for a loud bang, but we had no proper sound equipment.
剧本需要一声巨响，可我们没有合适的录音设备。
I pulled a metal tray from the cupboard and shook it beneath a thick cushion.
我从柜子里取出一个金属托盘，在厚坐垫底下晃了晃。
The sound was so soft it wouldn't disturb a sleeping cat.
声音轻得连睡着的猫都不会惊动。
Then the tray slipped out and hit the floor.
接着托盘滑了出去，砸在地板上。
We went silent.
我们一下子安静了。
There was the bang we wanted!
这正是我们想要的那一声巨响！
My cousin taped a note in neat letters to the cupboard: “Drop the tray from here.”
表亲用胶带把一张字迹工整的便条贴在柜子上：“从这个高度放下托盘。”
We put a phone on a shelf to record the sound.
我们把手机放在架子上录音。
Later, a classmate asked for an explanation of how we had made the thunder.
后来，同学问我们这雷声是怎么做出来的。
I showed her the tray.
我把托盘拿给她看。
She went home and tried it herself.
她回家后也自己试了一遍。

stories.title: The Blue Door
stories.picture: 街边的小书箱开着蓝门，门上系着细绳，里面整齐地叠着书。
paragraphs: A little book box stood opposite our bus stop.
公交车站对面有个小书箱。
Its plain blue door had lost its handle, so nobody could open it.
书箱有扇纯蓝色的门，门把手掉了，谁也打不开。
I got a piece of string from our kitchen cupboard to mend it until we could fit a proper handle.
我从厨房柜子里找了段细绳，把门暂时修好，等有空再装个合适的把手。
Inside, there was a neat pile of books on the bottom shelf.
里面最下面的搁板上整整齐齐地放着一摞书。
Beneath the pile, I found an envelope with no name on it.
我在书堆下发现一个没写名字的信封。
A receipt was tucked inside.
信封里塞着一张收据。
On the back of the receipt, someone had left a note: “Please take a book and leave one for the next reader.”
有人在收据背面留了张便条：“请拿一本书，再给下一位读者留一本。”
I taped the note to the door.
我用胶带把便条贴到了门上。
I left my favourite novel there.
我把自己最喜欢的小说留在了书箱里。
The next day, my favourite novel was gone, and a book about the moon sat in its place.
第二天，我最喜欢的那本小说被人拿走了，原处多了一本讲月球的书。

stories.title: A Light on the Stairs
stories.picture: 昏暗的楼梯间里，搁板上的一盏小灯照亮了台阶。
paragraphs: One evening, all the lights in our building went out.
一天晚上，我们楼里的灯全灭了。
I heard a bang in the corridor and found my neighbour sitting on the stairs.
我听见走廊里砰的一声，发现邻居坐在楼梯上。
He had slipped in the dark, and his foot was sore.
他在黑暗中滑了一跤，脚有些疼。
My aunt helped him while I looked in our cupboard.
姨妈去扶他，我跑去翻家里的柜子。
A small lamp and an envelope full of spare batteries were on the top shelf.
最高一层搁板上有一盏小灯和一个装着备用电池的信封。
We set it on a shelf opposite the stairs and taped a note to the wall beneath it: “Please leave the lamp on.”
我们把灯放在楼梯对面的架子上，在灯下的墙上贴了张便条：“请让灯一直亮着。”
By morning, two more lamps stood on the shelf.
到了早上，架子上又多了两盏灯。
Only then did I realise that the people upstairs had been in the dark, too.
我这才意识到，楼上的住户昨晚也摸着黑。
One little lamp had helped a lot of people.
一盏小灯帮到了不少人。

stories.title: A Photograph at Six
stories.picture: 傍晚，围栏旁的女孩拉着细绳，把小篮子升向二楼窗户。
paragraphs: I was assigned to take a photograph for a local exhibition.
我分到的任务是给本地展览拍一张照片。
Every evening at six, a girl by the fence opposite my window pulled on a long piece of string.
每天傍晚六点，我窗户对面的围栏旁都有个女孩在拉一根长细绳。
I could think of no explanation, so one day I went down to ask her.
我想不出她为什么这样做，于是有一天下楼去问她。
She put a finger to her lips.
她把手指放到嘴唇上。
I stayed silent and looked where she was pointing.
我安静地顺着她指的方向看去。
A basket rose past the fence and stopped beneath a second-floor window.
一只篮子越过围栏升了起来，在二楼一扇窗户下停住。
An old man at the window pulled the basket in.
窗边的一位老人把篮子拉了进去。
“That's Grandpa's supper,” the girl whispered.
“那是爷爷的晚饭。”女孩低声说。
“The doorbell disturbs the baby downstairs.”
“门铃会吵到楼下的小宝宝。”
I took one photograph and wrote a plain caption: “Waiting for supper.”
我拍了张照片，配上一句简单的说明：“等晚饭。”
When I showed her the picture, she gave me a quick nod.
我把照片拿给她看，她飞快地点了点头。

stories.title: The Jacket That Grew
stories.picture: 裁缝帮女孩检查绿外套接长的黄袖口，口袋上缝着一颗黄星星。
paragraphs: My niece loved a plain green jacket that had once belonged to her brother.
我外甥女喜欢一件纯绿色的外套，那是她哥哥以前穿过的。
By winter, its sleeves were too short, and one pocket had a hole.
到了冬天，袖子已经太短了，其中一个口袋也破了个洞。
She tucked the jacket into a bag and took it to a tailor.
她把外套塞进袋子里，拿去给裁缝看。
“Can you mend it and make the sleeves longer?” she asked.
“您能补好它，再把袖子做长一点吗？”她问。
The tailor gave a nod and took a tape measure from the shelf.
裁缝点点头，从架子上拿下一把软尺。
On a table lay two separate piles of cloth, one thick and one thin.
桌上分开放着两摞布料，一摞厚的，一摞薄的。
She added thick yellow cloth to both sleeves, with a neat row of stitches along each edge.
裁缝给两只袖子都接上厚黄布，沿着每条边工工整整地缝了一排针脚。
When we came back, a small yellow star covered the hole in the pocket.
我们回来时，口袋上的破洞已经被一颗黄色小星星盖住了。
The tailor slipped the receipt and the leftover cloth into an envelope.
裁缝把收据和剩下的布料塞进一个信封。
My niece held up her arms.
外甥女举起双臂。
“Look! It grew!”
“看！它长大了！”

stories.title: The Shop That Sold Nothing
stories.picture: 女孩抱着一本用胶带补过的书，打开架子上的蓝色零钱包，看到里面有张便条。
paragraphs: An advertisement on a fence said, “Bring something you no longer need.”
围栏上有一则广告：“带一件你不再需要的东西来。”
I used tape to mend the cover of a thick novel, then took it to the hall opposite the park.
我先用胶带把一本厚小说的封面粘好，再带着它去了公园对面的礼堂。
At the door, a woman handed me a receipt with the number one on it.
门口有位女士递给我一张写着数字一的收据。
Before I could ask for an explanation, she said, “You can take one thing from the shelves.”
我还没来得及问是怎么回事，她就说：“架子上的东西，你可以任选一件。”
On a shelf, behind a pile of old art equipment, I spotted a plain blue purse.
我在架子上的一堆旧美术用具后面瞧见一个纯蓝色零钱包。
A note tucked inside the purse said, “I made this when I was ten.”
零钱包里塞着一张便条，上面写着：“这是我十岁时做的。”
I chose the purse.
我选了零钱包。
At the check-out, a boy held up my book.
在结算处，一个男孩举起了我带来的书。
“This one's so good I read it twice,” I told him.
“这本特别好看，我读过两遍。”我告诉他。
He gave me a nod and handed over his receipt.
他点点头，交出了自己的收据。

stories.title: The Cup That Overflowed
stories.picture: 雨后的两个透明杯，一个放在围栏边，另一个放在树叶下。
paragraphs: My cousin and I wanted to see how much rain fell in our garden.
我和表亲想看看自家花园到底下了多少雨。
We had no proper equipment, so we put one cup by the fence and taped a ruler to it.
我们没有合适的设备，就在围栏边放了一个杯子，再贴上一把尺子。
At supper, the rain began with a bang of thunder.
晚饭时，雷声轰地一响，雨下了起来。
An hour later, the cup was full.
一小时后，杯子满了。
A second cup of the same size was almost empty.
另一个同样大小的杯子却几乎是空的。
We had left it beneath a tree.
我们把它放在树底下了。
My cousin said the difference seemed too big and asked for an explanation.
表亲觉得差得太多，问我这是怎么回事。
I looked up and realised that the thick layer of leaves had kept most of the rain out.
我抬头一看，才意识到密密的叶子挡住了大部分雨水。
We made a note on our chart and put the cups in separate spots out in the open.
我们在记录表上记了一笔，把杯子分开放在空旷处。
The next shower gave us almost the same reading in both.
下一场雨过后，两边的读数就差不多了。

stories.title: The Ball We Could Hear
stories.picture: 体育馆里，一名闭着眼睛的学生伸手等着滚来的球，两个运动包标出球门。
paragraphs: At a sports club, our instructor set two bags on the ground to make a goal.
在体育俱乐部，教练把两个包放在地上，当作球门。
He set a ball between them and rolled it towards us.
他把一个球放在两个包中间，朝我们滚过来。
We heard a bell inside it.
我们听见球里有铃铛声。
“This is proper equipment for players who can't see,” he said.
“这是给看不见的球员用的正规器材。”他说。
We stood in two separate lines and took turns closing our eyes and trying to stop the ball.
我们站成两列，轮流闭上眼睛，试着拦住球。
I could hear the bell until a loud bang from the opposite end of the hall made me turn my head.
我本来能听见铃声，直到礼堂另一头传来砰的一声，我转过头去。
The ball slipped beneath my hand.
球从我手底下溜了过去。
Then I realised why we had to stay silent.
这时我明白了为什么大家得保持安静。
Even a small sound could disturb a player who was listening for the ball.
哪怕一点声音，也可能干扰靠听觉判断球在哪儿的队员。
On my next turn, I listened and caught it.
下一轮轮到我时，我仔细听，接住了球。
My team waited until the bell stopped before they began to clap.
我的队友等铃声停了才开始鼓掌。

stories.title: What Counts as Next Door?
stories.picture: 带着一叠信封的访客站在院门旁，门口的男孩递给她一个梨。
paragraphs: Our street was planning a picnic, and I was assigned to invite the people who lived nearby.
我们这条街要办野餐，我负责邀请住在附近的人。
I wrote each address on a separate envelope, put them in a neat pile and tied the pile with string.
我把每个地址分别写在一个信封上，把信封整齐叠好，再用细绳捆起来。
At number eight, a woman read the note and asked whether the families behind the fence could come too.
到了八号，一位女士读完便条，问围栏后面的几户人家能不能也来。
I hadn't even realised there were houses back there.
我之前都没意识到后面还有房子。
The woman drew a map on the back of an old receipt.
那位女士在一张旧收据背面画了张地图。
“Go through this gate so you don't disturb the dog by the other one,” she said.
“从这道门进去，免得惊动另一道门旁边的狗。”她说。
I followed her map.
我照着她画的地图走。
At the first door, a boy gave me a pear before I could even ask his name.
在第一户门口，我还没来得及问名字，一个男孩就递给我一个梨。

stories.title: Music from a Tin
stories.picture: 公园长椅上，男孩弹着用饼干铁盒、木条和细绳做成的小吉他。
paragraphs: In the park, a boy tried to play a tune on an old biscuit tin.
公园里，一个男孩试着用旧饼干铁盒弹一段曲调。
He had found some string on a shelf in the equipment cupboard at home and made his own guitar.
他在家里器材柜的搁板上找了些细绳，自己动手做了把吉他。
When I sat down, one of his three strings slipped loose.
我坐下时，他的三根弦里有一根松脱了。
He tucked it through a hole in the tin, but the tin fell with a bang.
他把弦塞进铁盒上的一个孔里，铁盒却砰的一声掉到了地上。
I helped him mend it with a thick piece of string from my bag.
我从包里拿出一根粗绳，帮他修好了。
The new string gave a much lower note.
新弦发出的音低了许多。
He stayed silent for a moment, then played the same tune again.
他安静了一会儿，又弹起了同一段曲调。
This time, he used the low note at the end.
这回，他把那个低音用在了最后。
It sounded like someone saying goodnight.
听起来就像有人在道晚安。
